Summary

CELLxGENE: colon immune, 96 samples was analysed with the Single-cell RNA-seq workflow (version 1.0.0) on the LSMA Analysis Lab. To run the Single-cell RNA-seq analysis on this dataset and describe what it shows. In summary, the stages completed and their outputs are below. 4 point(s) are flagged under Limitations and should be read before the results are used.

Introduction

From a cell-by-gene count matrix to quality control, normalisation, dimensionality reduction, optional batch integration, clustering, cell-type annotation, pseudobulk differential expression, pathway analysis and optional advanced analyses. Built on Scanpy, with DESeq2, clusterProfiler and fgsea for statistics. The data analysed here is of kind 'sc_matrix'.

Aim

To run the Single-cell RNA-seq analysis on this dataset and describe what it shows.

Methods

Assembled from what each completed stage recorded. Check it against the parameter tables below before using it in a write-up.

Raw counts for 152,509 barcodes and 26,766 genes from 96 sample(s) were read from AnnData (H5AD).

Cells were filtered on genes detected, total counts and mitochondrial fraction (median ± MAD per sample); doublets: Scrublet, run separately per sample on cells passing QC; expected rate 0.8% per 1,000 cells unless set. 133,889 of 152,509 cells and 22,214 genes were kept.

Random seed: 42. Software: python 3.12.16; anndata 0.13.4; h5py 3.16.0; numpy 2.5.4; pandas 2.3.3; scanpy 1.12.5; scikit-learn 1.9.1; scipy 1.18.1; scrublet 0.2.3.

Analyses were run on the LSMA Analysis Lab (workflow 'scrna-seq' version 1.0.0).

Results

One section per stage, in the order they ran. The badge on each heading says how far its output can be taken: exploratory output describes the data, statistically supported output carries a test, and interpretation is a reading of either.

Stage 1 of 10

Data import Exploratory

The uploaded files are read into a single AnnData object: a cells-by-genes matrix of raw UMI counts, with a table describing the cells (sample, any metadata you supplied) and a table describing the genes.

Note. X did not hold raw counts; raw counts were taken from .raw.
Note. The genes were indexed by database identifiers, so symbols were taken from var['feature_name'] (26,766 of 26,766 genes). The original identifiers are kept in var['gene_ids']. Marker-based annotation, the marker tables and pathway analysis all need symbols.
Note. This looks like an unfiltered (raw) matrix that still contains empty droplets. The QC stage will remove low-count barcodes, but dedicated cell calling (Cell Ranger's filtered matrix, or EmptyDrops/CellBender upstream) is preferable.

How to interpret this stage

Check the number of cells and genes and the cells per sample. The barcode rank plot shows total counts per barcode in decreasing order: a filtered matrix shows a plateau, an unfiltered one shows a knee followed by a long tail of empty droplets.

Stage 2 of 10

Cell quality control Exploratory

For every cell three core metrics are computed: the number of genes detected, the total UMI count and the fraction of counts from mitochondrial genes. Cells with extreme values are removed, using thresholds computed separately for each sample. Scrublet then simulates doublets and flags cells that resemble them.

Note. Scrublet needs at least 100 cells per sample; skipped for: H106265_N, H180844_N1, H180844_N2, N11_Epi_A, N128208_E, N154787_E1, N16_Epi_A, N16_Epi_B, N178961_E, N17_Epi_A, N17_Epi_B, N18_Epi_A, N18_Epi_B, N20_Epi_A, N21_Epi_A, N21_Epi_B, N46_Epi_A, N46_Epi_B, N51_Epi_A, N51_Epi_B, N8_Epi_A, N8_Epi_B.

What this stage found

This stage recorded cells before: 152,509, cells after: 133,889, removed low quality: 17,996, removed doublets: 624, predicted doublets: 624 and genes before: 26,766.

This is shown in Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 5, Figure 6, Figure 7, Figure 8, Figure 9 and Figure 10.

The stage raised one warning, given in full below.

How to interpret this stage

Look at the violin plots per sample before trusting any threshold: good samples have similar distributions. The scatter of counts against genes should follow one trend. Expect to remove a few percent of cells. If a sample loses far more than the others, the sample itself may be the problem.

Discussion

What the run amounts to, drawn from the stages that carry a judgement. Every sentence below was written by the stage that reached it; none is a later interpretation.

This run describes the data rather than testing a hypothesis about it, so there is no verdict to draw together here. The Results describe what was measured.

The run raised 4 warnings, listed with the stages that raised them. They are part of the result, not notes beside it.

Everything above was produced by Single-cell RNA-seq on the data named in the Data section, with the parameters recorded under each stage. The Limitations section says what this design cannot show, and should be read before any of this is quoted.
